reviews.review: game suffers from extremely low performance

I've been playing a lot of ArcRunner lately, and I love it.

[TLDR:  If you want a solid cyberpunk rogue-style shooter where you can turn your brain off while you run around and shoot things without breaking your bank, you'll enjoy this.]

The combat is fast-paced, and satisfying.  It feels great to run, dodge, shoot, and blow things up.  The weapons, buffs, and their effects are quick to equip, and easy to understand.  The omission of a cover mechanic, and crouching is not necessarily a bad thing as it keeps the mechanics of the game simple, and straightforward.  Exercise all of your core shooter fundamentals while playing this, and you'll do fine as you run in and out of cover while taking out your opposition.  The dodge mechanic is a nice touch for getting out of particularly dangerous moments, or just for closing the distance a little faster for a shotgun blast.

The visuals for the game are pretty eye-catching.  This developer definitely went with the "less is more" approach and it shows.  The geometry and textures of the environments and character models are simple, but detailed enough to immerse you in this cyberpunk world.  The lighting and surface effects are where the visual polish really shines through.  Neon signs light the City arenas, the Space Dock floors are shiny, and sun rays break through the clouds above Eden.  Overall, the game looks great.

The sound effects and music are what you would expect from a sci-fi cyberpunk title like this, and not in a bad way.  The music has the new-age 80s synth sound to it, and each of the weapons have their fun distinctive "pew-pews" and "bang-bangs".  It's nothing groundbreaking, but it all fits the setting very well.

As far as unlockables go, you unlock the hacker class, and higher difficulty settings by simply playing through the game.  You can also unlock all of the weapons for early use on Stage 1 by using each one and eliminating X amount of enemies, or X amount of elites (bosses) depending on the weapon.  I haven't played multiplayer with friends yet, but I hear it's a blast.  The replayability of this game simply comes from whether or not you have the urge to blast your way through another run or not.  If you thoroughly enjoy the gameplay loop, you'll want to keep playing.

What's here is very solid and fun, but not without it's flaws.  The game crashed on me once, but I didn't lose any progress.  I was able to start my game back on the stage where I left off before the crash, so that was a relief.  Assault rifles feel kind of useless while SMGs are very strong.  The jumping is kind of floaty, but I'm not really sure if that's a bad thing or not; just something I noticed.  The boss fights are alright, but I prefer all of the fighting leading up to the bosses.  Make of that what you will.

This title and developer have a lot of potential to be something pretty damn awesome.

If I had to rate this game based on everything I've just said:
7.7 out of 10

This is definitely a fun one, and I got what I paid for.  I'm happy with it, and would definitely recommend.

Thank you for reading!
